Software8 min read

What makes software production-ready?

Production-ready software is correct, secure, observable, recoverable and maintainable. A checklist we use before any release.

By the collective · 29 July 2026

In this note

CorrectSecureObservableRecoverableMaintainableTalk about your workflow

Keep these in mind.

  • Working on a laptop is not production-ready.
  • You can't fix what you can't observe.
  • Test your backups by restoring them.

Correct

Automated tests cover the core flows, and they run on every change. Edge cases found in testing become permanent tests.

Secure

Access is role-based, secrets are never in code, dependencies are scanned, and data is encrypted in transit and at rest.

Observable

Errors are captured with context, key metrics are dashboarded, and someone is alerted before users notice a problem.

Recoverable

Backups run automatically and are restored on a schedule to prove they work. Releases can be rolled back in minutes.

Maintainable

Another engineer can understand, run and change the system using its documentation. If only one person can deploy it, it isn't production-ready.

A practical starting point—not a substitute for reviewing your own context, risks and requirements.
